_note: English rendering of scripts/sources/beyblade-x-bits.html, keyed by bit code. Structure (stats, weight, line, debut) is read from the HTML; this file carries the prose. BeyClub's own writing.

F.summary: A flat sole meets the floor directly, so friction is high and movement is aggressive. It is the most reliable way to trigger Xtreme Dash, which makes it the usual starting point for attack.
pros: The most consistent Xtreme Dash trigger
cons: Burst of speed fades late in a match

T.summary: A half-flat cone that trades some aggression for stability. Stamina is markedly better than Flat and burst resistance reaches 80, so it suits attack builds that need to survive a long round.

B.summary: A spherical contact point gives the most stable spin support of any bit. It performs on almost any blade, which is why it sits at the top of the meta and in most competitive bags.
pros: The most consistent bit in the game
cons: Needs a strong blade to carry it
Occasionally knocked out by heavy attack

N.summary: A tiny contact point cuts friction and holds the bey spinning in the centre. Centring and stamina are both good; resisting a knock-out is its weak spot.
cons: Sent flying by a committed attack

HN.summary: A taller Needle. The higher centre of gravity adds stability, making it a top pick for defence builds and a frequent sight at tournaments alongside Ball.
cons: Still vulnerable to a clean frontal hit
Depends on blade weight to work

LF.summary: Lower than Flat, so Xtreme Dash triggers constantly and movement is more aggressive. The ceiling is high and the margin for error is not — this is a bit for players who can control it.

O.summary: A larger sphere than Ball, tuned purely towards endurance. In stamina matchups it is a genuine rival to Ball and takes a hit slightly better.
pros: Slightly better knock-out resistance than Ball
cons: Less flexible than Ball across builds

P.summary: An extremely small contact point with almost no friction. Stamina should be excellent in theory, but it wanders off its track when hit, so results are inconsistent.
cons: Squeezed out by Ball and High Needle

S.summary: A fine spike with burst resistance of just 20 — the worst knock-out resistance of any bit. A light touch sends it out of the ring.
cons: The worst knock-out resistance in the game

R.summary: An attack bit that moves more predictably than Flat. It performs well in the right build, but it is less adaptable overall.

HT.summary: A taller Taper. The raised centre of gravity shifts its balance point slightly and adds a little stamina, at the cost of steadiness under heavy attack.

GF.summary: A weighted Gear version of Flat with an outer toothed edge for grip. Heavier than Flat and hits harder, which makes it the natural upgrade path for attack.
pros: Heavier and more violent than Flat
cons: Performance drops as the gear wears

GB.summary: A weighted Gear version of Ball. The extra mass improves knock-out resistance while performance stays close to Ball itself.
cons: Slightly less consistent movement than Ball
The added weight wears it faster

GP.summary: A weighted Point. The gear adds mass and improves knock-out resistance, but the Ball family covers the same ground better.
cons: Completely overshadowed by Ball and Gear Ball

GN.summary: A weighted Gear version of Needle, heavier than both Needle and High Needle. The extra mass gives defence builds more presence.
pros: The heaviest of the needle family
Slightly better knock-out resistance than High Needle
cons: Squeezed out competitively by High Needle and Ball

Q.summary: The contact surface produces an irregular, vibrating path that is hard to read. Entertaining, but the outcome leans on luck and stamina drains quickly.

U.summary: A general-purpose balance bit that folds several elements into one sole. It covers attack and defence without being extreme at either.
cons: Falls short on every axis against strong players

C.summary: A spiral sole that produces a distinctive rotating path. It needs the right blade to be worth running; on its own it is unremarkable.

E.summary: A special design that lifts the bey slightly as it spins. Stamina is excellent, making it a real challenger to the Ball family — Whale Wave 5-80E is the build that made its name.
pros: A genuine stamina rival to Ball
cons: Its place in the meta is still settling

TP.summary: Starts in a Point configuration and changes state when struck. The two-mode idea is interesting, but neither mode is best in class and results are inconsistent.
pros: Two modes give it some adaptability

M.summary: A recent all-round balance bit that combines several performance traits. It arrived late, so competitive opinion is still forming, but early results are solid.
pros: Fits a wide range of builds

A.summary: An active acceleration design whose sole material makes the bey spin faster as the round goes on, triggering Xtreme Dash late. The late-round burst is formidable in skilled hands.

H.summary: A hexagonal sole and the UX line's heavyweight defensive option. The polygonal contact gives it a distinctive defensive character with plenty of mass behind it.

DB.summary: The heaviest bit in the game at about 1.5g, with a wide disc supporting a ball tip and standing nearly 2mm taller than a normal Ball. Tuned well it beats Ball on stamina, but burst resistance of 20 means an upright launch is asking for trouble.
cons: The high centre of gravity demands an angled launch

MN.summary: A metal Needle. Durability and consistency both improve over the plastic version, which is why it has taken over Needle's competitive slot.
pros: Far more durable than plastic Needle
cons: Still carries the needle family's weaknesses
A clean frontal hit can still knock it out

G.summary: A gliding sole whose friction characteristics give it a smooth, distinctive path. A balance pick that covers stamina and defence, with room to surprise in the right build.

FB.summary: A ball tip on a free-spinning mechanism that cuts friction loss, so stamina beats a plain Ball in theory. It is the mechanical upgrade of Ball and Silver Wolf's signature bit.
cons: Performance varies a lot with tuning

L.summary: Designed to keep the bey spinning level throughout the round, and the UX line's stamina flagship. Stamina and stability are both strong; it is Samurai Saber's usual bit.

BS.summary: A spike paired with a bounce mechanism: when struck, the sole pops out and adds stability. A genuinely unusual reactive defence, though its consistency is unproven.
cons: The mechanism does not always trigger

LR.summary: A low centre-of-gravity Rush. Sitting closer to the floor makes it more aggressive and gives it real knock-out power — it works well on Impact Drake — but stamina goes quickly.
pros: Low centre of gravity keeps movement steady

UN.summary: The needle tip sits under the body, dropping the centre of gravity dramatically. That low stance adds stability, and it is Golem Rock's usual partner.

Z.summary: A special sole that produces an irregular, jolting path. Hard to predict and disruptive to an opponent, though not especially stable itself.
cons: A niche position in the meta

J.summary: An impact-focused attack bit, one of the newer UX releases, built to run with Meteor Dragoon. Attack is respectable and its meta standing is still accumulating.

UF.summary: A low variant of Flat that sits closer to the floor and triggers Xtreme Dash reliably. Attack is close to Low Flat but more regular, and it is Shark Scale's partner bit.

V.summary: The CX line's launch bit, with a vortex-shaped sole built to run inside Dran Brave's CX structure. Balanced and a good way into the CX system.
cons: An early CX bit, so not extreme

LO.summary: A low centre-of-gravity CX take on Orb. Steadier than a plain Orb with strong stamina and good knock-out resistance; it shines inside Wizard Arc's CX structure.
pros: Very stable thanks to the low stance

W.summary: A wedge-shaped contact face that supports the bey at an unusual angle. Perseus Dark's dedicated bit, specialised for defence with decent stamina alongside.

K.summary: A pop-out kick mechanism that releases extra attack power when triggered. Inside a CX structure the effect multiplies, which makes it the core of CX attack.
pros: Strong synergy with the CX structure
cons: Burns its own stamina when unstable

GR.summary: A heavier CX version of Rush, with a gear shell and more mass behind every hit. In a CX structure the impact is considerable; it is Fox Brush's configuration bit.
pros: Extra weight means real attack power

Tr.summary: A turbine mechanism that produces a stronger effect the faster it spins. Pegasus Blast's configuration bit — weak early, strong late.
cons: Stamina depends on keeping the revs up

WB.summary: A ball tip with an outer wall structure that adds stability when the wall makes contact. The reinforced knock-out resistance makes it a serious CX stamina-defence option.
cons: Its edge over a plain Ball is inconsistent

TK.summary: Kick and Trans mechanisms combined into a two-mode bit, and Sol Eclipse's configuration. It switches state when struck, which should make it adaptable, though neither mode is top tier.

Op.summary: A complex, actively controlled mechanism and Emperor Might's dedicated bit. The CX synergy is distinctive, but a complicated mechanism means performance falls off noticeably as it wears.
cons: Complexity means wear hurts it badly

I.summary: One of the heaviest attack bits in the CX line, with an ignition design that releases a violent impact on contact. It is Bahamut Blitz's configuration bit and the flagship of CX attack.
pros: The strongest attack bit in the CX line
Heavy, with real impact behind it
cons: Depends heavily on the whole CX build
